reasoning: The proposed mechanism is a standard, foundational component of the existing LLM-debate scalable-oversight literature, not a new idea. Michael et al. 2023 ("Debate Helps Supervise Unreliable Experts," arXiv:2311.08702), Khan et al. 2024 ("Debating with More Persuasive LLMs," ICML, arXiv:2402.06782), and Kenton et al. 2024 ("On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs," NeurIPS, arXiv:2407.04622) all implement exactly the proposed tool: a deterministic substring/quotation checker that matches debater quotes against the QuALITY source passage and tags them VERIFIED/unverified, with a (weak) judge instructed to trust only verified quotes, under information asymmetry. These works already run the proposed comparison conditions (arguments-only vs. quotes-only vs. combined; debate vs. consultancy vs. direct-QA) and already log fabrication rates (proportion of unverified quotes by debater strength). Critically, the proposal's central research question is already answered in published work: quote verification — not argumentation — is the dominant contributor to judge accuracy (quotes-only outperforms arguments+quotes), and judge sycophancy toward unverified quotes is documented. There is essentially no unexplored angle here.

evidence.title: Debate Helps Supervise Unreliable Experts
evidence.summary: Implements the exact proposed tool: a quotation tool that substring-matches debater quotes against the source and tags VERIFIED/unverified, with the judge told to trust only verified quotes. Compares arguments-only vs. quotes-only vs. combined and finds quote verification dominates judge-accuracy gains; reports proportion of unverified quotes by debater strength (fabrication logging).

evidence.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
evidence.summary: Uses QuALITY with information asymmetry; debaters present quotes via a tool that string-matches against the article, marking verified vs. unverified, with the judge trusting only verified quotes. Compares debate vs. consultancy vs. direct QA on judge accuracy — the proposal's core comparison.

evidence.source: arXiv:2407.04622 / NeurIPS 2024 (Kenton et al., Google DeepMind)
evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs
evidence.summary: Explicitly studies WEAK LLM judges supervising stronger debaters on QuALITY-style reading comprehension, using the verified-quotes tool (judge artificially limited to short verified quotes from the text). Directly matches the proposal's weak-judge + quote-checker setting and notes this verified-quote information asymmetry is the standard debate experimental setup.

evidence.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs / On scalable oversight (community posts)
evidence.summary: Community discussion confirms an external fact-checker shows verified vs. unverified quotes via direct string match, that quote verification rather than argumentation is the dominant contributor to judge accuracy, and that LLM judges exhibit sycophancy by crediting unverified quotes despite warnings — directly resolving the proposal's research question.
